title: What is Heteroskedasticity?
summary: This video explains the technical definition of heteroskedasticity, why it matters in regression analysis, how to detect it using residual plots and tests like the Goldfeld-Quandt test, and its effects on standard errors.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity
concepts.summary: Heteroskedasticity occurs when the variance of the error terms (or Y given X) is not constant across observations.

concepts.name: Homoskedasticity
concepts.summary: Homoskedasticity refers to the desirable condition where the error terms have a constant and even spread of variance across all values of X.

concepts.name: Standard Error
concepts.summary: In the presence of heteroskedasticity, standard errors are typically underrepresented and unreliable, leading to suspect t-values and p-values even though the regression coefficients remain unbiased.

concepts.name: Goldfeld-Quandt Test
concepts.summary: The Goldfeld-Quandt test is a statistical method used to detect heteroskedasticity by ordering data by an offending variable, splitting it into segments, running separate regressions, and comparing their error variances using an F-statistic.
